sermon.title: The Six Seals — Book of Revelation
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches on the first six seals of Revelation 6 and the sealing of God’s people in Revelation 7, warning that just as the Jews’ charts missed the first coming, end-time charts can miss the second. He reads the four horsemen from Scripture alone, argues the black horse is not famine and the pale horse’s power is limited, and says Christ’s return waits for the martyrs, the sealing of God’s people and a great harvest from every nation.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he gives “Matthew 13:14” for the abomination of desolation; that saying is in Matthew 24:15 and Mark 13:14 (Luke 21:20 is shown). He cites Hebrews 2:14 and later “Hebrews 2:12” for Jesus destroying him who had the power of death; that is Hebrews 2:14 (shown). The captions read “Visions 113” for “sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,” rendered Ephesians 1:13. His statements about named end-time authors and preachers (including that they made millions), about Chicago and Washington DC murder rates and gun laws, and about other churches and religious groups are his own and are not verified here. One name is given as the captions heard it, and several words are marked [unclear].

faqs.question: What defiles a person, according to him?
faqs.answer: He says it is things within that defile us, not what we eat or wear: “it’s what comes out those words and those actions that’s what defiles us.”

faqs.question: Why did the religious leaders worry that all would believe on Him?
faqs.answer: He says they wanted people to believe in their group and their doctrine, but “We’re supposed to be believing and trusting in and following Jesus Christ.”

faqs.question: How many books does he say the Bible mentions in heaven?
faqs.answer: He says the Bible tells us about eight books, including the book of life, the book of works and the book of remembrance.

faqs.question: Was part of Daniel’s sealed book fulfilled in 70 AD?
faqs.answer: He says the destruction of Jerusalem in 70 AD fulfilled Daniel, so at least part of Daniel’s sealed book was opened.

faqs.question: Who does he say is antichrist?
faqs.answer: He says the apostle John said there are many antichrists: those who oppose Christ and say He did not come in the flesh.

faqs.question: What does he say about guns and murder?
faqs.answer: He says “it’s not the gun that kills people,” and if you change the heart of a person you have control.

faqs.question: Why does he say end-time teachers make things look bad?
faqs.answer: He says “They want it to look bad because people like bad news”; trouble gets our attention.

faqs.question: Can Satan act without God’s permission?
faqs.answer: He says Satan “can do beans without God giving permission,” and Satan is ready and willing any time God will let him.

faqs.question: How does he say Christians renounce Christ today?
faqs.answer: He says that by saying sexual immorality is acceptable or that it is okay for Christians to divorce, “we just renounced the Bible”; we deny Him by our actions.

faqs.question: Is there a seven-year tribulation in the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says “Nowhere in the Bible does it say there’s seven years of tribulation”; they have to manufacture it out of Daniel.

faqs.question: What does the seal of the Holy Spirit guarantee?
faqs.answer: He says it is a guarantee that He will finish the good work He has begun in us; as long as he serves and seeks Him, He will get him to the goal.

faqs.question: Are only 144,000 going to heaven?
faqs.answer: He says no; the list of tribes even leaves out Dan and Ephraim, and “there’s an innumerable group of people up there in heaven.”

faqs.question: What is the second coming really about?
faqs.answer: He says it is about the power and revelation of Jesus Christ, “it’s not about the beast and the troubles in the seven years of tribulation it’s about the conquering Jesus.”
